skill.name: secrets-gitleaks
skill.description: Use Gitleaks guidance and templates to detect hardcoded credentials, prevent secret commits, build CI/CD scanning, and plan safe remediation.
skill.summary: Guides secret scanning workflows with Gitleaks configurations, hooks, CI templates, and remediation references.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are expected Gitleaks documentation, configuration examples, or CI templates rather than live secret access. I confirmed one unsafe troubleshooting command and added a high-confidence semantic finding for unredacted Gitleaks reports that can expose detected secrets in CI logs or artifacts. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unredacted Gitleaks reports are generated and retained in CI templates.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction to Gitleaks commands, avoid printing raw findings, restrict artifact access, and encrypt stored reports.

remediation.issue: A troubleshooting example uses xargs with sh -c on report-derived values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a small script that validates numeric lines and quotes file paths safely before reading context.

remediation.issue: Optional CI integrations use repository tokens and outbound notification services.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege token scopes and require users to review Slack and GitLab notification steps before enabling them.

semantic_findings.title: Unredacted Secret Reports in CI Templates
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub and GitLab templates generate Gitleaks reports without redaction and upload or retain them as artifacts. The GitLab incremental job also prints new-findings.json to logs, which can expose detected secret values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The report generation commands visibly omit redaction while artifacts and log output retain or print the generated reports. Gitleaks JSON findings can include secret material, so this is a credible exposure path.

medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The troubleshooting example pipes Gitleaks output into xargs and sh -c, embedding report-derived file and line values in a shell command. A crafted repository path could turn copied guidance into command injection.

content.value_statement: Hardcoded credentials create incident risk and compliance gaps. This skill helps teams add Gitleaks scanning, prevention, and remediation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains repository, directory, baseline, and incremental scans with Gitleaks.
Provides pre-commit configuration for blocking secrets before commits.
Includes GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for automated scanning.
Supplies strict, balanced, and custom Gitleaks configuration templates.
Maps secret scanning controls to PCI-DSS, SOC2, GDPR, OWASP, and CWE.
Provides remediation and false positive guidance for detected credentials.
limitations: Requires users to install Gitleaks and apply templates manually.
CI templates need review before production because scan reports may contain sensitive findings.
Does not rotate, revoke, or replace exposed credentials automatically.
Documentation references helper scripts that are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prevent Secret Commits
use_cases.description: Set up pre-commit checks that stop API keys, tokens, and passwords before code reaches the repository.

use_cases.title: Gate CI Pipelines
use_cases.description: Add Gitleaks scans to GitHub Actions or GitLab CI and fail builds when new secrets appear.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map secret detection workflows to compliance controls and document remediation actions for exposed credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use secrets-gitleaks to plan a first Gitleaks scan for my repository. Include scope, report handling, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Commit Protection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use secrets-gitleaks to design a pre-commit workflow that blocks secrets and explains safe bypass review rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use secrets-gitleaks to adapt the CI template for my platform. Include token scope, artifact security, and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Detection Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use secrets-gitleaks to create organization-specific Gitleaks rule guidance with allowlists, entropy thresholds, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add secret scanning before merge.
output: Recommended a Gitleaks CI gate for pull requests and default branch updates.
Identified report handling safeguards before artifacts are stored.
Listed credential rotation steps for any confirmed exposure.

output_examples.input: A repository has many legacy findings.
output: Suggested creating a baseline to separate existing findings from new issues.
Recommended staged remediation for high-risk credentials first.
Included review rules for false positives and allowlist changes.

output_examples.input: A security engineer needs custom secret rules.
output: Outlined rule design for organization-specific token formats.
Explained capture groups, entropy checks, and test coverage.
Added guidance for limiting broad allowlists.

best_practices: Use redaction for scan output and restrict access to all findings reports.
Rotate exposed credentials before removing them from code history.
Review allowlist changes with security owners and document the reason.
anti_patterns: Do not commit scan reports that may contain detected secret values.
Do not use broad allowlists that disable meaningful detection.
Do not treat removal from the current branch as credential remediation.

faq.question: Does this skill run Gitleaks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that users apply in their own repositories and pipelines.

faq.question: Can it remove exposed secrets from history?
faq.answer: No. It explains remediation workflows, but users must rotate credentials and run cleanup tools themselves.

faq.question: Which integrations are covered?
faq.answer: The package covers pre-commit, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, baseline scans, and custom configuration templates.

faq.question: Are Gitleaks reports safe to share?
faq.answer: Not by default. Reports can contain sensitive findings and should be redacted, encrypted, and access controlled.

faq.question: Can I add custom detection rules?
faq.answer: Yes. The custom configuration template explains rule patterns, entropy thresholds, capture groups, and allowlists.

faq.question: Does it support compliance work?
faq.answer: Yes. The references map secret scanning practices to PCI-DSS, SOC2, GDPR, OWASP, and CWE controls.
